name: Identity Kinds Benchmark, tier 1 (deterministic)
about: IKB-1. Recorded on AgentMemory 2.3.1 by the tier 1 harness (strategy/features/evidence-based-identity/validation/identity-kinds/IdentityBench.cs.txt), its own Neo4j 5.26, the token-hash embedder at 1024 dimensions. Reproduced unchanged on main at 68bbddb3 (22 Nov 2026, Neo4j 5.26.33): every row equal. The test in tests/AgentMemory.Tests.Integration/Services/IdentityKindsBenchmarkTests.cs runs the same cases and compares each row; a change that moves a row updates this file with its reason. Version 2 (26 Nov 2026, ER-KIT), re-recorded at feat/post-276-batch 635ddad4 with each arm on an empty store, twice, every row equal between the two runs. Why: the arms share the test's Neo4j, and recall and identity read across owners, so an arm measured what the arms before it had left there (2.3.1's harness ran all three in one store, in this order, and never emptied it). What moved: no verdict, separate things, wrong merges or last-mention join in any of the 402 rows; open proposals in 15 rows, all S02-later (rules 235 to 236: home 4 to 6, document 4 to 3; writer 174 to 197, 13 rows), which still depend on how many entities the other cases wrote (ER-OWNER-CROWDING: the candidate pool is read from the whole store before the owner filter) and will move again when that is fixed. Names in the profile block: IBP-1 (#271) shows each line once, so a split thing is named once (extra names: rules 142 to 9, writer 110 to 9; not compared by the test); team.S02-later and home.S02-later are named 0 times in all three arms now (previous was 1), not explained here. Version 3 (26 Nov 2026, ER-OWNER-CROWDING), re-recorded twice with the two runs equal row for row: identity's fuzzy and semantic routes now score the owner's own entities when the store-wide pool comes back full and short, so the cases of one arm (134 owners in one store) no longer crowd each other's candidates out. Moved: open proposals in 13 S02-later rows (rules 5, writer 8), rules 236 to 247 and writer 197 to 214; no verdict, separate things, wrong merges or last-mention join. The test Other_owners_records_leave_every_identity_row_of_an_arm_as_it_was now holds: an arm run again beside its first run's records gives every identity row unchanged.
